You know where the old foraging trails begin, west of Primeval Woods. The forest is yours — but the paths grow back. An Overgrown Forest Trail waits at Primeval Woods: hack it clear with a blade to open the way in. Left untended it regrows in about ten days, so keep your blade sharp. A portal will always take you straight to the forest if the trail closes on you.
Brush and bramble have swallowed the old trail into the foraging forest. Hack it clear with a blade, axe, shovel, or antler to open the way west.
Cut back the brush with a blade, axe, shovel, or antler to clear the trail. Opens the foot route to the foraging forest.
The trail into the foraging forest is open. Left untended, the brush will creep back over it in about ten days — keep a blade handy.
Regrowth: About 10 days. When the Regrowth bar fills, the trail becomes overgrown again and the foot route into the forest closes until you hack it clear once more.
The forest trail has grown over again.
Clumps of peanut pods just dug from the soil. Still caked in dirt — rinse them in water before shelling.
Found: Foraging in oak groves, pine forests, and clearings (spring–fall). Processing: Drag a water container onto the pods to rinse them, then use Shell to get raw peanuts.
Rinse the soil from the pods with water.
Clean peanut pods, ready to shell. Crack them open to get the raw peanuts inside.
Made from: Rinsing a Peanut Pod with a water container. Next step: Use Shell to crack open the pods and get raw peanuts. They spoil faster once wet, so shell them promptly.
The wet peanut pods have rotted.
Shelled peanuts, edible raw but better roasted. Rich in fat and protein, though they leave your mouth dry.
Made from: Shelling a Washed Peanut Pod. Uses: Eat raw for moderate nourishment, or place on a fire and use Roast for a richer nutritional boost. Keeps for about a month.
The raw peanuts have gone rancid.
Warm, fragrant peanuts roasted over a fire. Packed with fat and protein — a dense, satisfying meal, though you'll want water nearby.

Made from: Roasting Raw Peanuts on a fire (2 hours). Uses: Eat for a substantial fat and protein boost. High in calories, but very drying — have water on hand. Keeps for over a month. Grind: Grind with any grinding tool into Peanut Butter. Trail Mix: Combine with dried billberries (Cooking tab) for a travel ration.
The roasted peanuts have gone rancid.
Grind the roasted peanuts into peanut butter.
Cold-pressed oil extracted from raw peanuts, served in a clay bowl. Nutty and rich. Eat it, season food with it, or render it into lamp oil.
Crafted: By pressing 3 Raw Peanuts + Clay Bowl on a placed Oil Press. Uses: Eat directly (returns empty clay bowl), drag onto food to season, or render over a fire into lamp oil.
Crush 3 raw peanuts in the press and collect in a clay bowl to extract peanut oil.
Roasted peanuts ground into a thick, rich paste. Dense fat and protein in every bite — sticks to the roof of your mouth, so keep water close.
Made from: Grinding Roasted Peanuts with any grinding tool. Uses: Eat for a hearty fat and protein meal. Very drying — have water on hand. Keeps for two months.
The peanut butter has gone rancid.
Roasted peanuts tossed with dried berries — a light, dense ration made for a day on the trail.
Made from: 2 Roasted Peanuts + 2 Dried Billberries (Cooking tab). Uses: Eat on the go — solid calories and fat without the thirst of plain roasted peanuts. Keeps for two months.
The trail mix has gone stale and moldy.
Toss 2 roasted peanuts with 2 dried billberries to make 2 portions of trail ration.
